clinician.trajectory_summary: A 70-year-old male with a history of type 2 diabetes and prostate cancer in remission presented in October 2019 with a right leg DVT, followed by persistent fever and a widespread skin rash. Other symptoms included asthenia, weight loss, palpebral edema, laryngeal pain, hearing loss, episcleritis, dysphagia, progressive sensitive disorders in feet, muscle pain, and recurrent DVT. An initial skin biopsy (end 2019) confirmed Sweet's syndrome. Investigations at this time revealed an inflammatory syndrome (CRP 187 mg/L) and polyclonal hypergammaglobulinemia, while ruling out JAK-2 mutation, viral, and bacterial infections. By the end of 2020, a recurrence of asthenia, weight loss, skin eruption, and palpebral edema led to re-hospitalization. Due to this complex symptomatology and the patient's history of Sweet's syndrome, an investigation for a unifying explanatory autoinflammatory disease was initiated in early 2021. This led to genetic testing for a UBA1 mutation, which came back positive (p.Met41Val), establishing the diagnosis of VEXAS syndrome. Following the VEXAS diagnosis, high-dose corticosteroids were initiated in the ICU, leading to symptom stabilization. The patient was discharged from the ICU in February 2021 to internal medicine, where oral corticosteroids and subcutaneous Anakinra were continued. During this period, he experienced multiple severe infections and recurrence of Sweet's syndrome skin lesions during corticosteroid tapering. In May 2021, he underwent a right foot tarsometatarsal amputation due to distal necrosis and angioplasty procedures.
